hypotheses.justification: The proof uses hB in one place: it passes hB to `terminalRemainder_tsum_bound`. That call comes after `intro ... hV ...`, so hV : ∀ x, ‖V x‖ ≤ B is already in scope, and `(norm_nonneg _).trans (hV 0)` proves 0 ≤ B there. The rest of the proof is unchanged, and the U₀ chosen before the intro does not depend on hB. Degenerate case B < 0: then no V satisfies hV, so the inner implication holds vacuously for every U₀. The statement is therefore true for every B. hBT can be deleted as well, and the two deletions are independent.

The proof uses hBT in one place: it passes hBT to `terminalRemainder_tsum_bound`. That call comes after hT : ∀ x, ‖T x‖ ≤ BT has been introduced, so `(norm_nonneg _).trans (hT 0)` proves 0 ≤ BT there. U₀ is chosen without using hBT, so nothing else changes. Degenerate case BT < 0: hT cannot hold, so the conclusion holds vacuously. hB can be deleted as well, and the two deletions are independent.
